tools.name: spreadsheet_create
tools.description: Build a real .xlsx spreadsheet and deliver it as an in-chat attachment that opens NATIVELY in Cue's spreadsheet viewer. THIS IS THE ONLY correct way to produce ANY spreadsheet/Excel/.xlsx file — financial models, budgets, forecasts, P&Ls, cap tables, pricing models, expense reports, comparison sheets. NEVER build an xlsx by hand: do not write raw XML/OOXML, do not shell out via bash/host_bash to python (openpyxl/pandas/zipfile stdlib), node, apt, npm, or any package install to assemble a workbook. A hand-built file has no cached formula values, does not open in the native viewer, and forces the user through pointless tool-approval prompts — always call this tool instead. CRITICAL formula convention: any cell string beginning with "=" is written as a LIVE Excel formula (e.g. "=B2*C2", "=SUM(D2:D13)", "=Assumptions!B4") — every derivable value MUST be a formula, never a precomputed number, so the user can change an input and watch everything recalculate. This tool pre-computes and caches every formula result, so the file opens fully rendered in Cue's viewer and recalculates in Excel/Numbers/Sheets.

filename.description: Output filename, e.g. "saas-model.xlsx" (.xlsx appended if missing).

sheets.description: Worksheets in order. For financial models: sheet 1 = Assumptions (every driver as a labeled input), later sheets reference them by cell ("=Assumptions!B4").

rows.description: Array of row arrays. Each cell is a string, number, boolean, null — or a rich cell object {"value": <cell>, "format": "<Excel number format>", "bold": <bool>}. Strings (plain or in "value") starting with "=" become LIVE formulas.

column_widths.description: Optional widths per column, in Excel character units (e.g. [24, 12, 12]).

number_formats.description: Optional map of column letter → Excel number format, e.g. { "B": "$#,##0", "D": "0.0%" }.
